_meta.why: AI-TAX must compute both tax regimes from the user's actual tagged deductions and salary structure, and print the FY rules version on every result. Tax parameters change every Budget, so they MUST be a versioned data file (served by /v1/knowledge/tax), never hardcoded.
_meta.what: The FY2025-26 parameter table (§38.1) and the post-23-July-2024 capital-gains treatment (§38.2), plus the harvesting-alert rules (TAX-001/002).
_meta.result: The engine computes old-vs-new regime break-even in rupees and labels capital-gains lots correctly; every figure is stamped with fy_rules_version.
changelog: 2026-07-17 — Created from SRS v1.7 §38.1, §38.2. UPDATE every Budget and bump fy_rules_version.

2026-10-09 — Issue 13.4 built AI-TAX against this file and found it could not be computed from: NEITHER regime had a slab table, and §38.1 does not state one either. Added both (the new-regime table is corroborated by §38.1's own anchors — 30% above 24L, and tax at 12L taxable = 60,000 = the 87A rebate that makes 12L tax-free), plus the 4% cess, the 87A rebate amounts and the old-regime standard deduction. Capital-gains and harvesting rules moved out of prose into typed fields, with the sentence kept as `says` so the transcription can be checked. `fy_rules_version` is UNCHANGED at 2025-26.1: the law did not move, only this file's completeness. See ADR-0072.
_meta.scope_note: The engine never files taxes and links complex cases (property, foreign/RSU taxation) to a professional (TAX-002).

old_regime.slabs_note: Typed so an engine can read them. A rate is BASIS POINTS (MNY-002); `upto_inr` null means no upper bound. Boundaries are exclusive of the previous band and inclusive of upto_inr.

new_regime.slabs_note: Corroborated against §38.1's own anchors: the 30% band starts above 24L, and tax at 12L taxable is 20,000 + 40,000 = 60,000 — exactly the 87A rebate that makes 12L 'effectively tax-free'. Rates are BASIS POINTS (MNY-002).

break_even_engine.method: Compute both regimes from the user's actual tagged deductions + salary structure (basic/HRA/rent). Old regime wins only when utilised deductions exceed the computed break-even.
break_even_engine.output: The winning regime and the rupee margin, shown to the user.

capital_gains._typed_note: Issue 13.4 moved these out of prose and into fields an engine can read, the way issue 10.4 did for the vehicle KB. The sentences are kept as `says` so the reader can check the transcription. Rates are BASIS POINTS (MNY-002).

rules.says: STCG (<=12 mo) 20%; LTCG (>12 mo) 12.5% on gains above INR 1.25L/year, no indexation
Slab rate always - no LTCG benefit; engine labels lots accordingly
12.5% no-indexation, OR 20% with indexation if acquired before 23 Jul 2024 and lower - engine computes both
Capital gains fully exempt - flagged as the most tax-efficient gold route

surcharge_and_cess._source: Finance Act FY2025-26. Cess applies to every taxpayer; surcharge only above 50L.
surcharge_and_cess.cess_note: 4% on (tax + surcharge), after the 87A rebate. Applies in BOTH regimes. Leaving it out would understate every estimate by 4%.
surcharge_and_cess.surcharge_note: NOT modelled. Surcharge starts at 10% above 50L and rises in bands, and it comes with MARGINAL RELIEF, which needs a second computation at the band boundary. The engine flags that an estimate above this income is understated rather than quietly reporting a low figure (P-03).

rules.says: Unused INR 1.25L LTCG exemption approaching FY-end -> gains can be realised tax-free and cost basis reset.
Harvestable losses before 31 March (India has no wash-sale rule).
STCG->LTCG countdown when a planned sale is < 30 days from turning long-term.

harvesting_alerts.never: The alerts are GENERIC. The engine never names an instrument to sell (TAX-001).
